visual_profile.summary: GEGYjiji is a 26-year-old Chinese watercolor artist based between Tokyo and Beijing. Originally from Changsha (Hunan Province), she studied illustration and design at Beijing Fashion Institute. She paints urban atmosphere, domestic stillness, cats, interior light, and the quiet accumulation of memory. Her practice is illustration-community rooted — zine shops, art book publishers, and illustration fairs are her primary ecosystem; fine art galleries are secondary. She has N2 Japanese and a ~26k Instagram following, and is actively building toward publication collaborations and Tokyo exhibition presence.

practice_context.explanation: GEGYjiji's formation is at Beijing Fashion Institute (design/illustration), not a fine arts academy. Her online presence, publications, and first Japan exhibition (a group show organized by a Chinese ACG/illustration company) are all illustration-community contexts. Her ~26k Instagram following is an illustrator-community following, not a fine art collector following. This does not make fine art galleries wrong for her — her work is genuinely suited to gallery contexts — but it means the illustration/publishing ecosystem is her native territory and the higher-probability near-term path. Gallery track is a parallel development, not the primary one.
practice_context.scoring_instruction: When two opportunities have equivalent pipeline scores, the one in the illustration/publishing ecosystem should surface first. Gallery calls should not be suppressed — they remain valid and aspirationally correct — but artist book publishers, zine distros, illustration fairs, and bookshop galleries should consistently rank ahead of equivalent gallery open calls in Immediate Best Moves.

artist_statement.verbatim_source_ja: 中国人イラストレーター、湖南省出身、北京服装学院卒業。水彩画を得意とし、将来はイラストを描くコスチュームカメラマンになることを目指す。『defined Definition 02: A Documented Journey』や、きのこ王国とのオフライングループ展の制作に携わり、2021年10月に初のソロイラストレーション集『Colour Diary』を刊行。また2020年から毎日の水彩画を描き、それらは「diary」という名称で続けている。作品は、まるで北国を旅する列車のように、春夏秋冬に満ちあふれ、それらは暖かい日差しやそよ風を感じさせ、見る者に見慣れた街角や公園を散策するような感覚を覚えさせる。赤い壁、路地、プール、緑の池…ごく普通の日常を感動的なシーンに。
artist_statement.verbatim_source_context: Exhibition bio, Tide from China Part1, ACG_Labo, Tokyo, February 2023. First Japan exhibition.
artist_statement.verbatim_translation_en: Chinese illustrator, from Hunan Province, graduated from Beijing Fashion Institute. Specializes in watercolor, and aspires to become a costume photographer who also draws illustrations. Has participated in 'defined Definition 02: A Documented Journey' and offline group exhibitions with Kinoko Kingdom. In October 2021, published first solo illustration collection 'Colour Diary'. Since 2020, has painted daily watercolors, continuing a series called 'diary'. Works are like a train traveling through the north — filled with all four seasons, conveying warm sunlight and a gentle breeze, giving the viewer the sensation of strolling through familiar street corners and parks. Red walls, alleyways, pools, green ponds… transforming the utterly ordinary everyday into moving scenes.
artist_statement.synthesized_en: GEGYjiji is a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, originally from Hunan Province, who studied illustration and design at Beijing Fashion Institute. Since 2020 she has maintained a daily watercolor practice — a series called 'diary' — that her first solo collection, Colour Diary (October 2021), grew directly from. Her paintings move through the ordinary: red walls and alleyways, pools and green ponds, the interiors of rooms, the particular warmth of sunlight in a familiar street. Like a train traveling through the north, her work carries all four seasons and gives the viewer the feeling of walking through a place they half-remember. She made her first Japan exhibition in February 2023 as part of Tide from China Part1 at ACG_Labo in Harajuku, Tokyo.
artist_statement.tone_signal: The 'train through the north' passage in the ACG bio reads as artist-voice copy — lyrical, seasonal, grounded in specific images (赤い壁、路地、プール、緑の池). This register should be preserved when drafting on her behalf.
artist_statement.notable_gap: The bio mentions she 'aspires to become a costume photographer who also draws illustrations' (コスチュームカメラマン). This is a specific and unusual secondary ambition — not a contradiction of the painting practice but a distinct stated goal. Noted for accuracy; do not suppress this fact but it is not a primary career signal for Mochi's opportunity matching.

career_strategy.phase_note: Age 26, planning a deep-work year around 30. The next 4 years are for accumulation: exhibition history, publishing relationships, peer network, body of work depth. Tier 1-2 opportunities build this foundation. Tier 4 targets are tracked now and pursued later.
career_strategy.scoring_instruction: Weight Tier 1-2 opportunities higher for immediate recommendations. Tier 3 is neutral. Tier 4 entries must route to stretch_targets and never appear in Immediate Best Moves — they are future goals, not current actions.

daily_structure.description: Today's Focus on Mochi's page always contains exactly three items. Each maps to a tier.

items.label: Quick Win
items.description: Something completable right now. Low barrier. Builds momentum. Typically a Tier 1 action: sending a message, checking a venue's consignment policy, confirming a deadline.

items.label: High Impact Move
items.description: The most important action today. Requires real attention. Typically a Tier 2-3 action: drafting an introduction email to a relationship target, preparing a submission package, researching a specific open call.

items.label: Stretch Goal
items.description: One step toward a future target. Not urgent but strategically important. Typically a Tier 4 action or long-range move: researching RWS criteria, drafting an artist statement, preparing a portfolio body for a residency application.

tier_1.label: Ambient Visibility
tier_1.description: Low-barrier, low-pressure presence-building. Work enters circulation without requiring the artist to pitch or perform. Builds name recognition passively over time.
examples: zine shop consignment (Tacoche, Dig A Hole, etc.)
bookshop display and consignment (UTRECHT, Book and Sons, B&B, flotsam books)
café print sales and wall display
art book fairs and zine fairs (exhibiting, not just attending)
self-publishing and small press releases
online artist-book platforms

tier_2.label: Networking
tier_2.description: Active community engagement. Building relationships with peer artists, gallery owners, publishers, and spaces that will matter in 3-5 years. Presence and visibility in the Tokyo art community.
examples: group shows in artist-run spaces (3331, Design Festa Gallery, Gallery IYN)
open calls at accessible local galleries
community exhibitions and collaborative projects
artist talks, workshops, events
Tokyo watercolor and illustration community participation

tier_3.label: Credibility
tier_3.description: Institutional legitimacy. Exhibition history that carries weight on a CV and in future applications to Tier 4 opportunities.
examples: small institutional exhibitions (TOKAS, BankART1929, Youkobo Art Space)
café exhibitions with documentation or catalogue
regional gallery shows with curatorial framing
legitimate juried open calls (Jinny Street Gallery, Belladonna Art, Shoto Museum)
Japan Watercolor Society annual exhibition

tier_4.label: Prestige Targets
tier_4.description: High-difficulty, high-reward opportunities. Not for immediate pursuit — for the deep-work year at 30 and beyond. Track now so the application is informed when the time comes.
examples: Royal Watercolour Society Open Exhibition (UK)
American Watercolor Society Annual International Exhibition (USA)
Cité Internationale des Arts Residency (Paris)
Asian Cultural Council Fellowship
Printed Matter Art Book Fairs (NYC/LA)
Offprint (Paris/London)
Center for Book Arts (NYC)
Significant international galleries and institutions
